title: India Tightens Nepal, Bhutan Border Rules: Passport Now Needed for Third-Country Travel
excerpt: A Home Ministry amendment keeps direct India–Nepal and India–Bhutan travel passport-free but makes a Visa Manual identity document mandatory at immigration — and closes the route for using either neighbour as a passport-free bridge to a third country.
body:
• The Home Ministry has notified the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) (Amendment) Order, 2026, amending the 2025 exemption order under Section 33 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025.
  • Direct travel between India and Nepal or Bhutan stays passport-free, but Indian, Nepalese and Bhutanese travellers must now produce an identity document specified in the Visa Manual before an immigration officer and furnish any information the officer seeks.
  • An Indian travelling to or returning from any third country through the Nepal or Bhutan border must carry a valid passport and enter or exit only through a designated immigration post — the exemption no longer covers that route.
  • Nepalese and Bhutanese citizens who have boarded a flight or transited through China, Macau, Hong Kong or Pakistan must carry both a valid passport and a valid visa to enter or leave India.

The Ministry of Home Affairs on Thursday, November 5, notified the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) (Amendment) Order, 2026, introducing specific amendments to the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) Order, 2025, according to Times of India reporting of the notification. For the large number of Indians who cross into Nepal or Bhutan for family visits, work, pilgrimages and trade, the headline is narrow but practical: the passport-free arrangement survives, and an identity check now formally comes with it.

Who is affected, exactly

Three groups are covered by the travel clauses. Indian citizens travelling to or returning from Nepal or Bhutan are affected, as are citizens of Nepal and Bhutan entering or leaving India. A third group — Indians who use Nepal or Bhutan as a corridor to somewhere else — faces the strictest change. Travellers between India and other neighbours, and long-haul travellers who do not route through Nepal or Bhutan, are not touched by these clauses at all.

What changed, precisely

Under the amended order, Indian nationals travelling to or returning from Nepal or Bhutan by land or air will be required to produce any one of the identity documents specified in the Visa Manual before an immigration officer, and to furnish any information the officer seeks, ANI reported via NewKerala. Citizens of Nepal and Bhutan entering or leaving India by land or air carry the same obligation.

The carve-out is the operative change. The exemption "shall not apply to a citizen of India departing to or returning from countries other than Nepal or Bhutan through the Indo-Nepal or Indo-Bhutan border by land or by air. In all such cases, they shall be required to possess a valid passport and their exit from or entry into India shall be only through the designated immigration posts." In plain terms: Nepal and Bhutan can no longer be used as a passport-free bridge to a third country. The same logic applies in reverse for Nepalese and Bhutanese citizens — the exemption does not cover travel to or from a country other than Nepal or Bhutan, and those who have boarded a flight or transited through China, Macau, Hong Kong or Pakistan must possess both a valid passport and a valid visa.

The wider exemption list

The order also restates who is exempt from the requirements to hold a valid passport, travel document and visa for entering, staying in or exiting India. The list includes members of the Indian Navy, Army and Air Force travelling on official duty, together with family members accompanying them on government transport; registered Sri Lankan Tamil nationals who took shelter in India on or before January 9, 2015; and foreign crew members of military vessels visiting India for repairs, who must hold a Military Ship Repair Permit and valid military identity documents.

PTI reporting carried by News89 adds further categories: members of minority communities — Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians — from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who were compelled to seek shelter in India due to religious persecution, or fear of it, and entered on or before December 31, 2024, including those who entered without valid documents or whose documents have since expired, though they must obtain an appropriate visa for continued stay. The provisions also cover Tibetan nationals who entered under the specified permit arrangements, and Pakistani nationals who entered India on or before December 31, 2009 intending to settle permanently, under stated conditions. The amendment has been issued under Section 33 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025.

What to do next

If you are travelling directly between India and Nepal or Bhutan, carry one of the identity documents specified in the Visa Manual and be ready to present it to an immigration officer — the order ties the document list to that manual rather than naming documents in the notification itself, so check the current manual list before you travel. If any leg of your journey continues to a third country through Nepal or Bhutan, treat a valid passport as mandatory and plan the crossing at a designated immigration post. The change sits alongside India's broader overhaul of traveller paperwork, including the plan to cut visa form fields by around 70 per cent for foreign travellers.
